newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil current account gap at $6.8 bln in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Brazil current account gap at $6.8 bln in Q1.

text.p: Brazil posted a current account balance of payments gap of $6.836 billion in the first quarter of 1997, compared with a deficit of $3.43 billion in the same period last year, the Central Bank said.
The Central Bank did not give the value of the current account gap in relation to gross domestic product.
The Central Bank said in a statement foreign direct investment in the first quarter reached $2.899 billion against $1.261 billion in January-March period in 1996.

"It's worth pointing out the increase in the part of the current account deficit that is being financed by direct investment, passing from 38.8 percent in 1996 to 42.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997," the statement said.
The Central Bank also said net foreign reserves at the end of March were $58.12 billion, down slightly from $58.524 billion in February.
According to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable, foreign reserves were $58.98 billion in March versus $59.405 billion a month before.
The bank said the current account deficit was mainly due to a first quarter trade gap of $3.1 billion.

It said the services account registered a first quarter deficit of $4.396 billion, with interest payments on debt accounting for $1.039 billion and other transactions in the services account for the rest.
Net unilateral transfers from Brazilians overseas fell to $618 million from $864 million in the first quarter of 1996.
